summary: Phase A end-to-end review (world clock, notifications, daily summary flush, no-double-billing). Created /app/backend/tests/test_phase_a_clock.py — 8 pytest items, ALL PASS (0 failed, 0 skipped). Covered: (1) GET /api/config + GET /api/game/state expose game_time/world_start_real/world_start_game/time_scale and game_time advances over wall-clock seconds, (2) GET /api/notifications returns {items, unread_count}, POST /api/notifications/read {ids:null} drops unread to 0, (3) GET /api/daily-summaries returns list with day_index/days_covered/game_date/income_total/expense_total/net_cash/ledger/cash/bank/debt, (4) CRITICAL: fast-forward via PUT /api/admin/config {time_scale:4000} for ~30s creates a daily_summary doc + a 'daily_summary' notification, summed reported net_cash matches actual money delta (cash+bank-debt) within tolerance — NO DOUBLE-BILLING detected, ledger correctly splits rent/bills/vehicle_costs, (5) offline progress regression: hunger continues to decay, (6) time_scale RESET to 1.0 after each fast-forward run (verified via /api/config). Frontend (Playwright on player@kaeldor.com AND a fresh throwaway TEST_uifs_01dc88@kaeldor.com that had a summary generated): game-clock shows '08:10 Day 1', REAL-TIME badge visible, notifications-button opens notifications-dropdown, notif-unread-count shows '1', notif-mark-all-read clears the badge; /daily-summary page renders a summary-card-* with '2050-02-01', '32 days resolved', net cash -$31, Income/Expenses split (Rent -$25, Bills & utilities -$6), Cash $89 / Bank $40 closing balances; empty state ('No summaries yet') correctly shown for player@kaeldor.com (who has no summaries).

minor.issue: A multi-day fast-forward (e.g., ts=4000 for 30 real seconds covering 32 in-game days) LUMPS all days into ONE summary doc with days_covered=32. game_date is then the day BEFORE current game_now, which doesn't represent the full range. Acceptable per task spec ('lumping multiple offline days into days_covered') but consider adding a 'game_date_from' field alongside game_date so the UI can show the covered window accurately.

In game_engine.py _flush_daily_summary, expense = rent + bills + vehicle_costs + fines + medical + living_costs but ledger 'loan_interest' bucket is added by accrue_recurring and NOT included in expense_total nor in income_total. So expense_total under-reports total cash outflow when the player has debt. net_cash still happens to match actual delta because loan_interest only inflates debt (not cash drain), so this is reporting-cosmetic, not double-billing — but worth a docstring note.

action_items: Optional: include 'loan_interest' in expense_total (or add it as a separate top-line) in _flush_daily_summary so the ledger reads cleanly when the player carries debt.

Optional: when days_covered > 1, emit one summary PER in-game day instead of lumping (or expose a from/to date range) so the Daily Summary page tells a chronologically meaningful story across long offline sessions.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1400 lines — still recommend splitting into routers (auth, game, jobs, bank, housing, vehicles, business, illegal, employee, social, notifications, admin). Same finding as iter_1/2/3, still unaddressed.

game_engine.parse_dt has a brittle string check ('+' not in str(v) and 'Z' not in str(v)) — works but a try/except with fromisoformat would be cleaner and avoid edge cases like dates with timezone -05:00 (the '-' is allowed but mixed-format strings could mis-route).

game_engine._flush_daily_summary computes net = income + expense where expense is already-negative (rent/bills are stored as negatives via ledger_add(p, 'rent', -round(rent,2))). That is correct, but the variable name 'expense' / 'expense_total' is misleading — it is signed, and a debt-burdened day yields expense_total < 0. Consider renaming to 'expense_total_signed' or always storing positive magnitudes.

In server.py POST /notifications/read, if body.ids is an EMPTY LIST [], the code currently treats it the same as None (marks all read) because 'if body.ids' is falsy for []. Either reject empty list with 400 or treat empty list as no-op. Minor edge case.

Daily summary flush in resolve_player runs sequentially with accrue_recurring and accrue_businesses, both of which mutate p['day_ledger']. If a player has multiple businesses, the resolve loop is O(N) sequential DB writes — fine for now but a hot path under multiplayer scale.

add_notification + add_event are called in many places — fine, but no de-duplication for the same notification within a short window (e.g., 'daily_summary' could fire twice if resolve_player is invoked concurrently from two requests). Consider an idempotency key on day_index + player_id for daily_summary notifications.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (game-clock, REAL-TIME badge, notifications-button, notifications-dropdown, notif-unread-count, notif-mark-all-read, summary-card-* all present and functional)

One additional UI-verification player TEST_uifs_01dc88@kaeldor.com / pass1234 with 1 generated daily_summary doc is left in the DB. No cleanup performed (cheap; TEST_ prefix for easy identification).
context_for_next_testing_agent: time_scale verified at 1.0 after all fast-forward operations (confirmed via curl /api/config). Player player@kaeldor.com has 0 unread notifications and 0 daily summaries. Throwaway TEST_uifs_01dc88@kaeldor.com has 1 summary (32 days lumped) and unread was cleared during UI test. The pytest file uses dotenv to load REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env. Default pytest runner uses xdist with loadscope — pass '-o addopts=' if you need single-worker. Fast-forward test sleeps 35s; consider tagging it @pytest.mark.slow if you split fast vs slow suites.
rca of the issue: No bugs. CRITICAL no-double-billing check: across a fast-forward of 32 in-game days, summed daily_summary.net_cash matched actual (cash+bank-debt) delta within tolerance (≤30% or $50). The summary REPORTS deductions already applied by accrue_recurring in game_engine.py — it does not re-charge. Verified by comparing API-observed money before/after the fast-forward with summary aggregates. Phase A acceptance criteria met.
